summary: Canso range lights: a front and rear pair of wooden towers guiding ships into Canso Harbour's south entrance since 1905.

light.note: Front light per the Coast Guard list (fixed red, 11.9 m, 13 nm); rear light fixed red, focal height 28.5 m. LighthouseFriends and NSLPS record a yellow characteristic from 1968 or 1992.

access.note: Grounds and towers closed (LighthouseFriends). Rear tower stands behind a seaside building on Union Street, in Canso.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives fixed yellow from the 1968 floodlighting; NSLPS dates fixed yellow to 1992; the current Coast Guard list gives fixed red. The record's F R matches the current list.
NSLPS marks both lights as not operating; the Coast Guard list gives both as active and year round. The record's active status follows the Coast Guard list.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-28. Checked against the Coast Guard list (both lights F R, year round, focal heights 11.9 m and 28.5 m, range 13 NM, structure heights 10.1 m and 13.8 m), NSLPS (began and lit 1905; automated by 1993; still operating: no), LighthouseFriends (both pages), and the Marine reports (scan pp. 43, 46, 35, 229 read in the local corpus; printed pp. 28, 30, 222 confirmed). The 1905 contract, the 32 ft front tower, the 1968 change and the Clara wreck (under the Canso heading, scan 229) match. The keeper W. J. Mathews: LighthouseFriends and the Marine keepers' table of 1909-10 (scan 166, printed 159) both give appointment 17 Dec 1904, so the story's date stands. The 1914-15 Marine table entry 'W. J. Matthews, Dec. 17, 1901' (matched by column position, against another station) is not used and was not checked on the page image. Bill Ringer (NSLPS, 1986-1996) conflicts with NSLPS's own automation date of 1993; the story says the sources do not settle it. NSLPS's elevation reductions (front 46 to 40 ft, rear 108 to 97 ft, 1964-68) are not used. The Clara wreck is recorded at the harbour entrance by the life-saving section; the range lights are not mentioned there, and the story says so. The Canso Harbour front and rear range lights (CCG 674, 674.2, on the north breakwater) are a different pair and are not used. No Chronicling America search was run for this station.
